overview: This one-page file consists of a State Department list-of-papers or cross-reference sheet concerning Japanese news-gathering activity in Mexico. It indexes an April 26, 1944 military attaché report, numbered 2078, about Kirjiro Watanabe, a Japanese newspaperman living in Mexico City, and summarizes his denial of allegations arising from an article in the Central American press; the underlying report is not included in the surviving text.

subfiles.title: List of papers concerning Japanese news-gathering agencies in Mexico
subfiles.about: The sheet indexes military attaché report no. 2078 concerning Japanese newspaperman Kirjiro Watanabe and allegations reported in the Central American press.
subfiles.summary: This filing sheet identifies the subject as Japanese news-gathering agencies operating in Mexico and records an April 26, 1944 military attaché item numbered 2078. Its abstract describes Kirjiro Watanabe as a Japanese newspaperman residing in Mexico City and states that he denied allegations associated with a Japanese employee that had appeared in the Central American press. The referenced report or press article is not reproduced on this page, and part of the abstract is obscured by faulty OCR.

interest: Although the substantive report is absent, the sheet provides a useful archival trail linking wartime U.S. military reporting, Japanese press activity in Mexico, and press allegations circulating in Central America. It is also evidence of how the State Department indexed individual journalists and cross-referenced intelligence or press reports across its decimal files.
